sections.overview: The cobbler wobbegong is a bottom-dwelling carpet shark found off southern and western Australia.
sections.identification: Rows of rough, wart-like tubercles and dark blotches across the back help identify it.
sections.habitat: It occurs on rocky reefs and weedy seabeds in coastal waters, to at least 35 metres deep.
sections.diet: Its feeding habits are poorly documented; reference sources suggest it takes bottom-dwelling invertebrates and fishes.
sections.behavior: The sources describe it as reef-associated but provide little detail on its day-to-day behavior.
sections.reproduction: It is presumed to be ovoviviparous, but little is known about its reproduction.
sections.ecology: Australian fisheries reports record it as a minor bycatch species; catches in South Australia are minimal and it is not retained there.
sections.conservation: The Australian government report records a global IUCN category of Least Concern, while noting that population trends are unknown.
